_note: Nicolas watches from the US. TMDB returns every country in one call, so a film not on his services at home may still be on one of them abroad, reachable over a VPN — including Canal+ in France, which he already does. Canal+ therefore needs no special-casing any more: France is simply one more VPN option.
_listedNote: Ranking services by film count is the wrong criterion for a subscription picker — it surfaces library and arthouse services carrying hundreds of old films (Kanopy 376, Criterion 374, Philo 203) and pushes Netflix into the tail. `listed` is Nicolas's actual subscriptions, confirmed 2026-08-19. Everything else is grouped as 'Others'. These are also the only services searched for abroad, since a VPN is pointless for a service he does not pay for.
_vpnNote: Only these countries are ever suggested. The preference order matters (France first, since that VPN route already works for Canal+), but so does the hard limit: without it the picker offered "Netflix Angola" for Shawshank, because it fell back to whatever country was alphabetically first. A suggestion he cannot act on is worse than none. These are the regions consumer VPNs actually serve well. US is included as a target too: it is only ever suggested when he is NOT there (the same-country guard handles that), and from France it is the only route to Peacock.
_homeNote: Countries Nicolas actually watches from. These keep a FULL provider list so the grey "Others" bucket is correct in each; every other country keeps only his own services, since the only question elsewhere is whether a VPN could reach it. Adding a country here requires a re-fetch and grows the payload, so keep the list to places he is really in.
